messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall SREs: elevated p99 latency detected for /v1/generate-stream (us-west1). p95=320ms p99=2.8s; error-rate up 1.2%. Investigating tokenizer / preproc path. [link to metrics]
Aj Patel: oncall here. Confirming spike on dashboards, seeing a clear tail at tok-preproc stage. p99 for streaming tails correlates with preproc queue growth.
Maria (SRE): +1 seeing backlog on preproc workers, cpu steal on preproc-pool-1. Any recent deploys to preproc or prompt-template service?
Sandeep Rao: I rolled out template-optimizer v1.3 earlier today (09:12 UTC) — it changes tool-schema expansion ordering and enables JSON_MODE by default for nested tool calls. Reverting now as a precaution.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback template-optimizer v1.3 -> v1.2 by @sandeep (deploy id: d-20260315-99). ETA rolling pods 6 -> 3 mins.
Aj Patel: Good. Meanwhile can we reduce concurrency on streaming workers to avoid long tail amplification? Also toggling prompt prefetch cache to hit-only mode.
Kyle (eng-runtime): Increasing preproc worker replicas now: `kubectl scale deployment preproc-pool --replicas=12 -n inference-prod` — doing a staged bump.
Zoe (CS): Any customer-facing impact yet? We have one support ticket flagged for slow responses in the sample app. Customer A experiencing repeated stalls at ~8s.
Maria (SRE): Impact: few production customers experiencing increased latency for streaming responses; internal SLO p99 (2s) breached intermittently. No data loss; mainly tail stalls during tokenization of large prompt templates and JSON-mode tool expansion.
Sandeep Rao: Rollback completed. template-optimizer v1.2 is back in prod. Observability note: the JSON_MODE toggle increases prompt-construction CPU by ~1.6x for complex tool schemas.
deploy-bot: Rollback finished: all pods returned to v1.2 (d-20260315-99)
Aj Patel: After rollback, preproc queue length started to drop. p95 improving to ~180ms, p99 still around ~1.6s on some long templates.
Kyle (eng-runtime): I've enabled KV tokenizer prefix cache for high-latency routes as a hotfix: `PATCH /config/service/preproc { prefix_cache: true }`. This should cut repeated template tokenization cost.
Maria (SRE): Recording mitigation steps for postmortem: 1) rollback template optimizer 2) scale preproc-pool to 12 3) enable prefix cache 4) temporary concurrency cap on streaming workers.
Zoe (CS): Notifying customers: sending a short update to affected accounts saying we saw increased streaming latencies, root cause in preproc templates, mitigation in progress.
Aj Patel: Looking at traces: the expensive span is `prompt_builder.expand_tool_schema` for nested tool calls in JSON mode; CPU stays hot for ~600-800ms per request and blocks the event loop for streaming chunk emission.
Sandeep Rao: Action item: add a cheap pre-check to limit nesting depth for JSON_MODE or fallback to simple expansion when depth > 3. I'll open a ticket and a small patch for canary tomorrow.
Kyle (eng-runtime): For immediate safety I pushed a rate-limit rule to routing: route heavy-tool-schema traffic to dedicated preproc instances with higher concurrency limits to protect default pool.
Maria (SRE): Oncall handoff in 20m to @Sandeep; if p99 falls back to <1s we can close incident. Please capture metrics snapshot (pre-rollback vs post-rollback) and add to incident doc.
Aj Patel: Confirming p95=160ms p99=890ms after hotfixes (observed 4m after rollback + cache). Keeping an eye on streaming stalls; will paged-notify if re-escalation needed.
Zoe (CS): Sent customer messages, linking to status page. Customers appreciate the quick rollback note.
Sandeep Rao: Added ticket INF-3245 to improve prompt-builder with guarded expansion and incremental streaming-friendly expansion. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml.
Maria (SRE): Final note before handoff: main risk was JSON_MODE enabling deeper schema expansion which amplified per-request CPU and queued work, tipping streaming tails past SLO. Mitigations: rollback, scale, caching, routing isolation.
Aj Patel: Handoff to Sandeep for followups. I'll remain available for questions. Closing paging for now. :white_check_mark:
